dora-sorrentino.name: Dora Sorrentino
dora-sorrentino.cv: Dora Sorrentino is a Neapolitan voice specialist with a background in singing and piano. She debuted in the title role of Madama Butterfly in Siena in 2021. A member of the Puccini Festival Academy 2020/21, in 2018 she debuted as Fiorilla in Il Turco in Italia for the international co-production The Magic of Opera for the Rossini 150 celebrations at the Italian Cultural Institute of London. Recent engagements include the UK tour as Berta in Il Barbiere di Siviglia for Barefoot Opera, the title role in Lucrezia Borgia for the presentation of the new critical edition at the Conservatorio di Napoli, and Giannetta in L’Elisir d’amore at Ras de Terra, Spain. She was a member of the Opera Studio 2018/19 of the Teatro Coccia in Novara, the Gstaad Menuhin Festival and the Nice Académie d’été, and has sung as soloist in Carmina Burana, Pergolesi’s Stabat Mater and a Verdi Choir Gala with the Lyric Choir of Cremona and Piacenza. She won the 2018 Simone Alaimo ‘Il bel canto’ competition, debuting as the Contessa d’Almaviva in Le nozze di Figaro at the Etna Opera Festival 2018.

marghe.name: Margherita Pucillo
marghe.now: Vocal coach; soprano, formerly Teatro San Carlo, Naples.
marghe.cv: Soprano Margherita Pucillo studied at the Conservatorio San Pietro a Majella in Naples and at the Scuola di Musica di Fiesole in Florence with Professor Ettore Campogalliani (teacher of Pavarotti and Freni). She has won numerous singing competitions, including the ‘Voltolini’ in Mantua, the ‘Tito Schipa’ in Lecce, the ‘Maria Caniglia’ in Sulmona, the ‘G. Verdi’ in Parma, the ‘V. Bellini’ in Caltanissetta and the ‘Carlo Coccia’ in Novara, and was a finalist in the ‘Luciano Pavarotti’ competition. She made her debut at the Teatro San Carlo in Naples in Il Rosario by Jacopo Napoli, later singing the title role in Puccini’s Madama Butterfly there, as well as La Rondine and Orff’s Carmina Burana. She has sung Adina in L’elisir d’amore in Lecce and Suzel in Mascagni’s L’amico Fritz in Novara and Alessandria. She has taught music to young inmates at the state prisons of Nisida and Airola, and singing and operatic repertoire to the young members of the Sancarlini Academy at the Teatro San Carlo. After years in the Teatro San Carlo Choir she continues her concert activity with the Coro Polifonico Flegreo, the Enrico Caruso Academy and the Coro delle Consonanze in Piacenza. Her commitment to young singers has made her a point of reference for the new generations of Neapolitan students; her latest project is a music-therapy course at the Don Bosco and San Gennaro hospitals in Naples.

novati.name: Claudio Novati
novati.now: Coordinating conductor of the Halle State Orchestra (Staatskapelle Halle).

borisov.name: Svetoslav Borisov
borisov.now: First Kapellmeister and Deputy General Music Director, Anhaltisches Theater Dessau.
borisov.cv: Bulgarian-German conductor Svetoslav Borisov has been First Kapellmeister and Deputy General Music Director at the Anhaltisches Theater Dessau since the start of the 2025/2026 season, having previously held the same position for several years at Theater Magdeburg. He is also Artistic Director of the Austrian chamber orchestra CON FUOCO. From 2013 to 2015 he was Assistant to General Music Director Steven Sloane and conductor of the Bochumer Symphoniker, and until 2016 Chief Conductor of the Varna State Opera, which later appointed him Principal Guest Conductor. In October 2023 he was nominated for the Opernwelt Award in the Conductor category for his Ariadne auf Naxos. In 2026/2027 he conducts Mozart’s Le nozze di Figaro, Janáček’s Jenůfa and the world premiere of the ballet Mythen der Liebe in Dessau, returns to Kraków Opera for a new Faust, and makes his debuts at the Konzerthaus Berlin (December 2026) and with the Münchner Symphoniker (summer 2027). Recent productions include La bohème in Münster, Die Zauberflöte in Wiesbaden and Sofia, Turandot in Kraków and Le Corsaire at Istanbul State Opera; in Dessau he has conducted Don Giovanni, Così fan tutte, La bohème and Swan Lake. His repertoire also includes Aida, Falstaff, La traviata, Eugene Onegin, Carmen, Roméo et Juliette, Salome, Fidelio, Die Fledermaus and Der fliegende Holländer.

ianone.name: Massimo Iannone
ianone.now: Vocal coach; formerly vocal coach at the Puccini Festival Academy.
ianone.cv: The name of Maestro Massimo Iannone is synonymous with passion, dedication and success in the world of opera. His career spans more than three decades of unrelenting commitment to training new generations of singers. It began at the Conservatorio San Pietro a Majella in Naples, where he studied singing and piano and perfected his technique under Maestro Ettore Campogalliani and the great tenor Alfredo Kraus, before building his career as a singer. His debut came soon, in the leading role of Offenbach’s Orphée aux enfers, after which he specialised in the eighteenth-century repertoire in major theatres and international festivals. From 2020 to 2023 he was a vocal coach at the Puccini Festival Academy. His masterclasses have reached every corner of the globe — from London to Paris, Berlin to China, Japan to Australia, the United States to Singapore, and India, where he gave the ‘Recitar Cantando’ Lectio Magistralis at the Italian Institute of Culture in New Delhi. Among his honours are the Premio Caruso, the Premio ‘Una vita per la musica’ and the Premio Thomas Schippers, and his appointment as Honorary Professor at the University of Handan, China.

temesi.name: Mária Temesi
temesi.now: Vocal coach; dramatic soprano, Hungarian State Opera.
temesi.cv: Mária Temesi, a dramatic soprano, studied opera and classical singing in Budapest and, on graduating, immediately received permanent contract offers from the opera houses of Budapest and Saarbrücken. At the age of 24 she made her debut at the Hungarian State Opera as Elsa in Wagner’s Lohengrin, conducted by Giuseppe Patanè. That same year her international career began — in Dresden, Berlin and Nice, and then at many of the world’s leading houses. She won two major international competitions: the SBRAC in Rio de Janeiro (1981) and the Pavarotti Competition in Philadelphia (1985). As a permanent member of the Hungarian State Opera she has given memorable performances across the Verdi, Puccini, Mascagni, Cilèa, Wagner and Richard Strauss repertoire — among them Desdemona, Elisabetta, Leonora, Tosca, Santuzza, Adriana Lecouvreur, Elsa, Sieglinde, Brünnhilde, Senta and Ortrud. She was a permanent guest at the Opéra de Nice (1984–1990), the Semperoper Dresden (1985–1990) and the Komische Oper Berlin (1987–1989). In 2016 the President of Hungary awarded her the Knight’s Cross of the Hungarian Order of Merit for her outstanding dramatic-soprano roles.

des-aubris.name: Zenaida des Aubris
des-aubris.now: Managing Director of the Opera Managers Association International.
des-aubris.cv: Zenaida’s early work took her to San Francisco Opera, where she was involved in casting and artistic administration with Kurt Herbert Adler. Over the course of her career she has worked as an agent and has been the personal manager of noted professionals such as Jean-Pierre Ponnelle and Lorin Maazel. For Zubin Mehta she served as General Project Director of Turandot in the Forbidden City, conducted by Maestro Mehta and directed by Zhang Yimou, televised to more than fifty countries. A former Intendantin of the Hangzhou Grand Theatre, she now advises music competitions and schools, and recent graduates on how to manage themselves and start their careers, through her company Opera Career Advice.

taddeo.name: Angelo Taddeo
taddeo.now: Artistic Director of the Puccini Festival.
taddeo.cv: Angelo Taddeo is a conductor, artistic director and opera producer whose career has taken him from the podium to the helm of opera festivals across Europe. Trained in the classics and in advanced composition, he graduated in Band Instrumentation in Italy and in Choral Conducting in Romania, then studied conducting with Maestro Nicola Samale. A long career as conductor and manager followed, with performances throughout Italy and Europe alongside orchestras including the Kraków Symphony Orchestra, the MÁV Symphony Orchestra of Budapest, the Israel Camerata Jerusalem, the Cyprus Symphony Orchestra, the Strings of La Scala, the Hermitage Orchestra of St Petersburg and the Moscow Symphony Orchestra. He then devoted himself to opera production, staging nearly twenty titles from Aida, Tosca, Turandot and La traviata to Puccini rarities such as Edgar and Le Villi, working with conductors and directors including Bruno Aprea, Gianluigi Gelmetti, Yuri Alexandrov and Michele Placido, and presenting recitals with great voices such as Montserrat Caballé, José Carreras, Renato Bruson, Leo Nucci and Katia Ricciarelli. His festival leadership includes the Abbazia di Casamari opera festival (artistic director and producer, 2012–2014), the Rousse Opera House seasons (2013–2015) and Taormina Opera Stars at the Teatro Antico (2015).

bockstiegel.name: Thomas Böckstiegel
bockstiegel.now: Director of the Artistic department and Head of Planning, Staatstheater Cottbus.
bockstiegel.cv: Thomas Böckstiegel is Director of the Artistic department and Head of Planning at the Staatstheater Cottbus. From the 2018/19 season he was artistic director and co-director of opera and musical theatre at the Theater und Orchester Heidelberg together with Ulrike Schumann, with whom he also led the festival »Winter in Schwetzingen«. Born in Solingen, he studied Theatre and Musicology at the Ruhr-Universität Bochum and the Folkwang Universität der Künste. His theatre career began during his studies at the RuhrTriennale in 2004, first in dramaturgy and later in the artistic management of the festival under Gerard Mortier and Jürgen Flimm. He went on to work in management at the Stadttheater Dortmund (2008/09), the Aalto-Theater Essen (2009–2016) and the Bühnen der Stadt Wuppertal (2016–2018), and was a guest lecturer in cultural management at the Ruhr-Universität Bochum. He regularly gives workshops and audition training for opera singers in Germany and abroad and sits on the juries of international singing competitions.

costabile-cisco.name: William Costabile Cisco
costabile-cisco.now: Playwright, director and costume designer; founder of Teatri della Psychè, Varese.
costabile-cisco.cv: A playwright, director and costume designer, William G. Costabile Cisco founded the Teatri della Psychè theatre company in Varese in 2002, debuting the following year with Euripides’ Hippolytus; his work in drama focuses on the revision of classics — especially Greek and Roman tragedy — and on crossover between genres. He graduated in 2015 from the National Academy of Dramatic Arts ‘Silvio D’Amico’ / Verona Opera Academy, and has since joined to his theatrical vocation a great passion for opera, studying and working with Lorenzo Mariani, Pier Francesco Maestrini, Denis Krief and Davide Livermore. In 2020 he directed in Novara the première of Cinque cerchi in un quadrato, the first Italian opera written on boxing; since 2023 he has worked with the rural opera festival of Villanueva de la Vera in Spain, staging L’elisir d’amore, La sonnambula (2024) and Il barbiere di Siviglia (2025), and in 2024 directed Donizetti’s Dalinda at the Baxter Theatre in Cape Town. Since 2018 he has been one of the most prolific writers for gbopera.it, a leading Italian opera and drama magazine.

demichele.name: Mariagrazia De Michele
demichele.now: Musicologist; PhD candidate, Conservatorio ‘L. Boccherini’, Lucca.
demichele.cv: Since 2024 Mariagrazia De Michele has been pursuing a PhD in Library Science and Musical Bibliography at the Conservatorio ‘L. Boccherini’ in Lucca, researching the personal collections of the Lucca composers Gaetano Luporini (1865–1948) and Gaetano Giani-Luporini (1936–2022). In 2023 she completed a specialisation in Artistic Vocology at the Conservatorio di Milano ‘Giuseppe Verdi’, and in 2019 earned a Master’s degree in Musicology from the University of Rome ‘Tor Vergata’; her training began at the Conservatorio di Benevento (Bachelor’s in Accompaniment, 2017). She studied classical singing and was a member of the Choir of the Teatro dell’Opera di Roma. Professionally she has worked as a music cataloguer in the libraries of the Conservatori of Como and Milan and at the Accademia of Teatro alla Scala. She presented her research at the Camaiore Sacro conference (2025) and at the IAML Congress in Thessaloniki (2026).

sorrentino.name: Ambra Sorrentino
sorrentino.now: Founder and CEO of Opera Co-Pro, London.
sorrentino.cv: Awarded Best CEO for the UK in 2020 and 2022 as CEO and founder of Opera Co-Pro, the Italian opera manager Ambra Sorrentino is an Expert Member of the European Commission for Culture. A former Artistic Consultant of Teatro Grattacielo in New York, she was Director of the artistic department of the Allee Theater / Hamburger Kammeroper, and has worked for Teatro San Carlo in Naples, Teatro Goldoni in Livorno, the Puccini Festival, Oper Leipzig, Stadttheater Ingolstadt, Theater Magdeburg and the Anhaltisches Theater Dessau. She is Artistic Director and Casting Manager for Opera La Vera in Spain and Director of Business Development of the Athens Philharmonic Orchestra, and has been Visiting Professor at the Sorbonne in Paris, HEMA in Prague, LUMSA in Rome, the Catholic University of Milan, the University of Salerno and the University of Ostrava. Recent projects include Handel’s Partenope at the Teatru Manoel in Malta, the world premiere of Donizetti’s Dalinda at the Berlin Konzerthaus and Opera UCT, the world premiere of the musical Callas & Onassis for the Varna State Opera, and the staged recital ‘Per sogni e per chimere’ (Stadttheater Ingolstadt in co-production with the Gärtnerplatztheater Munich).
